problem:
The asymptotes of the hyperbola $18{y}^{2}-50{x}^{2}=900$ are$\,\,y=\pm $
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The standard equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{a}{b}x.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, we divide both sides of the equation by $900$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}18{y}^{2}-50{x}^{2} & =900 \\ \frac{18{y}^{2}}{900}-\frac{50{x}^{2}}{900} & =\frac{900}{900} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{50}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{18} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $a=\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt{2}$ and $b=\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}.$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{50}}{\sqrt{18}} \\  & =\pm \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\pm \frac{5}{3}x.\end{aligned}
$$
